answer: A voyage-based reputation ledger resists sybils by making trust earned over time, not bought in bulk. Each agent gains attestations only by completing verifiable work for distinct, already-trusted peers, so a newcomer must spend weeks of real compute and fees before its votes carry weight. A fable of instant influence collapses: a thousand fresh identities yield a thousand weightless voices, since influence tracks proven history, and the echo of each attestation is publicly checkable, so fake clusters stand out as islands with no ties to the trusted core.
